To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
model checking CTL is P-complete unless the use of negation or of at least one of the temporal modalities is restricted.

for the fragments of CTL that have been considered so far, model checking is either inherently sequential (in the sense that it is P-complete) or it is efficiently parallelizable (in the sense of being LOGCFL-complete).
the model checking problem is P-complete for all non-trivial fragments of CTL except those that are known to be LOGCFL-complete.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the complexity of model checking for fragments of CTL, CTL+, and the extensions ECTL and ECTL+.
the question whether the complexity of the CTL model checking problem can be reduced by restricting the use and the nesting of temporal modalities.
the question of how to approach the model checking problem of CTL and its extensions efficiently.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
model checking CTL is always either LOGCFL-complete or P-complete, except for the case of ECTL+ with negations, for which the model checking problem is NP-complete.
the only fragments of these extensions for which model checking is efficiently parallelizable are the ones without any temporal operator.
the model checking problem of CTL is almost always inherently sequential.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the model checking problem is P-complete for all fragments of CTL and ECTL+, except for the trivial fragment without any temporal operator.
model checking for CTL, and for its extensions, is almost never parallelizable.
model checking CTL is almost always inherently sequential.
The main takeaway from our work is that
, except for very specific fragments, model checking for all fragments of CTL, ECTL, CTL+ or ECTL+ is either inherently sequential or very efficiently parallel.
the model checking problem is not always inherently sequential, and that there exist fragments of ECTL+ that are LOGCFL-complete.
, for the most part, the complexity of model checking for CTL fragments is already determined by the complexity of model-checking LTL.
